title: Diffusion
competency: Apply the particle nature of matter to explain diffusion and its everyday effects.

keywords.def: The mixing and spreading out of a substance because its particles move. Particles go from high to low concentration.
How crowded the particles of a substance are in a place.

en.text: Diffusion is the mixing and spreading out of a substance because its particles move. Particles go from where they are crowded to where they are few. Diffusion is very fast in gases, slower in liquids and very, very slow in solids.

screens.title: A smell in the class
screens.ask: Someone opens perfume in one corner of the class. Who smells it first?
screens.after: Students near the bottle smell it first. The perfume particles spread out slowly to the rest of the room.

screens.title: Experiment 2.1: simple experiment on diffusion
paras: Open a bottle of perfume in one corner of the room.
Record how long it takes students at different distances to smell it.
Add 2 or 3 drops of ink to a beaker of water. Watch the colour spread.

screens.caption: A drop of ink slowly colours all the water in a beaker.

screens.title: 2.1.4 Diffusion
paras: The mixing and spreading out of a substance because its particles move is called diffusion.
It is the net movement of particles from high concentration to low concentration.

screens.title: Fast or slow?
table: Very fast: particles move quickly in all directions
Smell of hot sizzling food reaches us far away
A drop of ink colours a beaker of water
Very, very slow: particles hardly move

screens.title: Diffusion in daily life
paras: Tea: a tea bag in hot water colours the water.
Perfume spreads from one part of a room to the rest.
A drop of food colouring colours a glass of water.
An open soda bottle goes flat: carbon dioxide spreads into the air.

screens.title: Diffusion around us
screens.ask: Tap each one. What spreads, and where to?
items: Tea particles leave the bag and colour all the water.
Perfume particles spread from one part of the room to the rest.
One drop colours a whole glass of water.
Carbon dioxide spreads out into the air. The soda goes flat.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The mixing and spreading out of a substance because its particles move. Particles go from high to low concentration.
How crowded the particles of a substance are in a place.

screens.text: Diffusion: in diffusion, particles move from …
screens.why:
At first the perfume particles are crowded near the bottle: high concentration.
Far away there are few: low concentration.
Moving particles spread from crowded places to less crowded places.
So diffusion goes from high to low concentration.
screens.clue: Where are the perfume particles crowded at first?

screens.title: Put in increasing order of the rate of diffusion
screens.why:
Solid particles hardly move: diffusion is very, very slow.
Liquid particles slide past each other: slower than in a gas.
Gas particles move fast in all directions: very fast.
So the order is solid → liquid → gas.
screens.clue: Which state has the fastest particles?
screens.text: Put the states in increasing order of the rate of diffusion (slowest first).
True or false: a tea bag in hot water colouring the water is an example of diffusion.
screens.why:
Tea particles start crowded inside the bag.
They move out into the water, where there are few.
Spreading out because particles move is diffusion.
So the statement is true.
screens.clue: Do the tea particles spread out?

screens.text: Diffusion in daily life: an open bottle of soda goes flat. Why?
opts: Carbon dioxide diffuses out into the air
screens.ans: Carbon dioxide diffuses out into the air
screens.why:
The soda holds a lot of carbon dioxide gas: high concentration.
The air has little carbon dioxide: low concentration.
The gas particles spread from the drink into the air.
So the soda goes flat: carbon dioxide diffuses out.
screens.clue: Where is the gas more crowded: in the drink or in the air?

screens.text: Diffusion and heat: Almaz puts one drop of ink in cold water and one in hot water. Which colours the water first, and why?
opts: Both the same: ink does not move
Neither: ink cannot diffuse in water
screens.why:
Step 1: hot water particles have more energy.
Step 2: they move faster and push the ink particles around more.
Step 3: faster motion means faster spreading.
So the hot water is coloured first.
screens.clue: Which postulate is about heat and speed?

screens.title: The particle model
steps: All matter is made of tiny particles.
The particles move all the time.

screens.text: Particle model: what happens to particles when matter is heated?
screens.why:
Heat is a form of energy.
Particles that gain energy move faster.
So heated particles move faster.
screens.clue: Think of hot and cold water.

items.ask: Exercise 2.3, word box: you smell deodorant in the classroom after someone sprays it in the hallway. The ___ moves from high concentration to low concentration.
items.why:
The deodorant was sprayed in the hallway.
What travels to your nose is its scent (smell) particles.
Answer: scent.
items.clue: Word box: diffusion, low, scent, high.

items.text: Exercise 2.3: the scent moves from ___ concentration in the hallway to ___ concentration in the classroom.
items.why:
It was sprayed in the hallway, so its particles are crowded there: high.
The classroom has few at first: low.
Diffusion goes from high to low.
Answer: high … low.

items.ask: Exercise 2.3: the scent spreading from the hallway into the classroom is an example of ___.
items.why:
The scent particles move and spread out.
Spreading from high to low concentration is diffusion.
Answer: diffusion.

items.title: Arrange in increasing order of the rate of diffusion
items.why:
Solids: particles hardly move, so diffusion is very, very slow.
Liquids: particles slide past each other, so diffusion is slower.
Gases: particles move fast in all directions, so diffusion is very fast.
So: solids < liquids < gases.
items.text: Arrange solids, liquids and gases in increasing order of the rate of diffusion (slowest first).

test.ask: Key word: the spreading out of a substance because its particles move is called ___.
test.why:
Particles of a substance are always moving.
So they mix and spread out from high to low concentration.
This process is called diffusion.

test.text: Rate of diffusion: in which state is diffusion fastest?
test.why:
Gas particles are far apart and move fast in all directions.
Liquid particles move slower; solid particles hardly move.
So diffusion is fastest in a gas.

test.text: True or false: diffusion in solids is very, very slow.
test.why:
Solid particles are packed tightly.
They only vibrate in place and hardly move.
So other particles can barely spread through a solid.
The statement is true.

test.text: Diffusion: which of these is NOT an example of diffusion?
test.why:
Diffusion: particles spread out from high to low concentration.
Food smell, ink in water and tea in hot water all spread out.
Water freezing to ice is a change of state: nothing spreads out.
So water freezing is not diffusion.

test.text: Diffusion in gases and liquids: why does the smell of cooking wat reach the next room faster than ink spreads in a cup of water?
opts: Gas particles move faster than liquid particles
test.ans: Gas particles move faster than liquid particles
test.why:
The smell of wat reaches us as a gas.
The ink spreads in a liquid.
Gas particles move faster than liquid particles.
So diffusion in the air is faster than in the water.
